		<h1 class="post-title" id="post-8242">A remark on the lonely runner conjecture</h1>
		<p class="post-metadata">13 May, 2015 in <a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/category/expository/" rel="category tag">expository</a>, <a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/category/mathematics/mathca/" rel="category tag">math.CA</a>, <a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/category/question/" rel="category tag">question</a> | Tags: <a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/tag/arithmetic-progressions/" rel="tag">arithmetic progressions</a>, <a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/tag/lonely-runner-conjecture/" rel="tag">lonely runner conjecture</a> | by <a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/author/teorth/" rel="author">Terence Tao</a>		</p>
	</div>
	<div class="post-content">
		<p>
 The <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonely_runner_conjecture">lonely runner conjecture</a> is the following open problem:
</p>
<blockquote><p><b>Conjecture 1</b>  Suppose one has <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cgeq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cgeq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cgeq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n \geq 1}" class="latex"> runners on the unit circle <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}}" class="latex">, all starting at the origin and moving at different speeds. Then for each runner, there is at least one time <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{t}" class="latex"> for which that runner is “lonely” in the sense that it is separated by a distance at least <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B1%2Fn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B1%2Fn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B1%2Fn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{1/n}" class="latex"> from all other runners. </p></blockquote>
<p></p>
<p>
One can normalise the speed of the lonely runner to be zero, at which point the conjecture can be reformulated (after replacing <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex"> by <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%2B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%2B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%2B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n+1}" class="latex">) as follows:
</p>
<blockquote><p><b>Conjecture 2</b>  Let <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_1,\dots,v_n}" class="latex"> be non-zero real numbers for some <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cgeq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cgeq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cgeq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n \geq 1}" class="latex">. Then there exists a real number <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{t}" class="latex"> such that the numbers <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Btv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ctv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Btv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ctv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, <p>
This conjecture has been proven for <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+7%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+7%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+7%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n \leq 7}" class="latex">, but remains open for larger <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex">. The bound <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\frac{1}{n+1}}" class="latex"> is optimal, as can be seen by looking at the case <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_i%3Di%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_i%3Di%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_i%3Di%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_i=i}" class="latex"> and applying the <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet%27s_approximation_theorem">Dirichlet approximation theorem</a>. https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{t \in {\bf R}}" class="latex"> for which </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle+%5C%7Ctv_1%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C%5Cdots%2C%5C%7Ctv_n%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D-%5Cvarepsilon&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle+%5C%7Ctv_1%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C%5Cdots%2C%5C%7Ctv_n%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D-%5Cvarepsilon&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle+%5C%7Ctv_1%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C%5Cdots%2C%5C%7Ctv_n%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D-%5Cvarepsilon&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle \|tv_1\|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}},\dots,\|tv_n\|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \geq \frac{1}{2n}-\varepsilon" class="latex"></p>
<p> for any <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarepsilon%3E0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarepsilon%3E0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarepsilon%3E0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\varepsilon>0}" class="latex">, but it has proven to be quite challenging to remove the factor of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{2}" class="latex"> to increase <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\frac{1}{2n}}" class="latex"> to <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\frac{1}{n+1}}" class="latex">. (As far as I know, even improving <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\frac{1}{2n}}" class="latex"> to <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%2Bc%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%2Bc%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%2Bc%7D%7B2n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\frac{1+c}{2n}}" class="latex"> for some absolute constant <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bc%3E0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bc%3E0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bc%3E0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{c>0}" class="latex"> and sufficiently large <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex"> remains open.)</p>
<p>
The speeds <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_1,\dots,v_n}" class="latex"> in the above conjecture are arbitrary non-zero reals, but it has been known for some time that one can reduce without loss of generality to the case when the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_1,\dots,v_n}" class="latex"> are rationals, or equivalently (by scaling) to the case where they are integers; see e.g. Section 4 of <a href="http://www.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=1853254">this paper of Bohman, Holzman, and Kleitman</a>.
</p>
<p>
In this post I would like to remark on a slight refinement of this reduction, in which the speeds <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_1,\dots,v_n}" class="latex"> are integers of <em>bounded size</em>, where the bound depends on <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex">. More precisely:
</p>
<blockquote><p><b>Proposition 3</b>  In order to prove the lonely runner conjecture, it suffices to do so under the additional assumption that the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_1,\dots,v_n}" class="latex"> are integers of size at most <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BCn%5E2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BCn%5E2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BCn%5E2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n^{Cn^2}}" class="latex">, where <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BC%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BC%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BC%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{C}" class="latex"> is an (explicitly computable) absolute constant. (More precisely: if this restricted version of the lonely runner conjecture is true for all <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+n_0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+n_0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+n_0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n \leq n_0}" class="latex">, then the original version of the conjecture is also true for all <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+n_0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+n_0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn+%5Cleq+n_0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n \leq n_0}" class="latex">.) </p></blockquote>
<p></p>
<p>
In principle, this proposition allows one to verify the lonely runner conjecture for a given <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex"> in finite time; however the number of cases to check with this proposition grows faster than exponentially in <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex">, and so this is unfortunately not a feasible approach to verifying the lonely runner conjecture for more values of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n}" class="latex"> than currently known.
</p>
<p>
One of the key tools needed to prove this proposition is the following additive combinatorics result. Recall that a <em>generalised arithmetic progression</em> (or <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BGAP%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BGAP%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BGAP%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{GAP}" class="latex">) in the reals <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{{\bf R}}" class="latex"> is a set of the form </p>

<p>
We write </p>

<p> for some <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cleq+n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cleq+n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cleq+n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{d \leq n}" class="latex">, <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bw_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cw_d%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bw_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cw_d%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bw_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cw_d%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{w_1,\dots,w_d}" class="latex">, and <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BN_1%2C%5Cdots%2CN_d+%5Cgeq+0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BN_1%2C%5Cdots%2CN_d+%5Cgeq+0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BN_1%2C%5Cdots%2CN_d+%5Cgeq+0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{N_1,\dots,N_d \geq 0}" class="latex">. <p>
We now need an elementary lemma that allows us to create a “collision” between two of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_1,\dots,a_n}" class="latex"> via a linear projection, without making any of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_i}" class="latex"> collide with the origin:
</p>
<blockquote><p><b>Lemma 5</b>  Let <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%5Ed%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%5Ed%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%5Ed%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_1,\dots,a_n \in {\bf R}^d}" class="latex"> be non-zero vectors that are not all collinear with the origin. Then, after replacing one or more of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_i}" class="latex"> with their negatives <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B-a_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B-a_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B-a_i%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{-a_i}" class="latex"> if necessary, there exists a pair <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%2Ca_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%2Ca_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i%2Ca_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_i,a_j}" class="latex"> such that <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j+%5Cneq+0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j+%5Cneq+0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j+%5Cneq+0%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_i-a_j \neq 0}" class="latex">, and such that none of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_i-a_j}" class="latex">. </p></blockquote>
<p></p>
<p>
<em>Proof:</em>  We may assume that <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cgeq+2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cgeq+2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cgeq+2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{d \geq 2}" class="latex">, since the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cleq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cleq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd+%5Cleq+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{d \leq 1}" class="latex"> case is vacuous. Applying a generic linear projection to <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{{\bf R}^2}" class="latex"> (which does not affect collinearity, or the property that a given <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_k%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_k%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_k%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_k}" class="latex"> is a scalar multiple of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_i-a_j%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_i-a_j}" class="latex">), we may then reduce to the case <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd%3D2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd%3D2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bd%3D2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{d=2}" class="latex">.
</p>
<p>
By a rotation and relabeling, we may assume that <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_1}" class="latex"> lies on the negative <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bx%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bx%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bx%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{x}" class="latex">-axis; by flipping signs as necessary we may then assume that all of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_2%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_2%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_2%2C%5Cdots%2Ca_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_2,\dots,a_n}" class="latex"> lie in the closed right half-plane. <p> where the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+w_1%2C%5Cdots%2C%5Ctilde+w_%7Bd-1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+w_1%2C%5Cdots%2C%5Ctilde+w_%7Bd-1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+w_1%2C%5Cdots%2C%5Ctilde+w_%7Bd-1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\tilde w_1,\dots,\tilde w_{d-1}}" class="latex"> are real numbers that are linearly independent over <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+Q%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+Q%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+Q%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{{\bf Q}}" class="latex">, whose precise value will not be of importance in our argument. As we are assuming inductively that the lonely runner conjecture holds for <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn-1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn-1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn-1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n-1}" class="latex">, we conclude (after deleting duplicates) that there exists at least one real number <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+t%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+t%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+t%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\tilde t}" class="latex"> such that </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \| \tilde t \tilde \phi(a_1) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}}, \dots, \| \tilde t \tilde \phi(a_n) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \geq \frac{1}{n}." class="latex"></p>
<p> We would like to “approximate” <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\phi}" class="latex"> by <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\tilde \phi}" class="latex"> to then conclude that there is at least one real number <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{t}" class="latex"> such that </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+t+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+t+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+t+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+t+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+t+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+t+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \| t \phi(a_1) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}}, \dots, \| t \phi(a_n) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \geq \frac{1}{n+1}." class="latex"></p>
<p> It turns out that we can do this by a Fourier-analytic argument taking advantage of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BC_0+n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BC_0+n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BC_0+n%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n^{C_0 n}}" class="latex">-proper nature of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BQ%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BQ%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BQ%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{Q}" class="latex">. Firstly, we see from the Dirichlet approximation theorem that one has </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cleq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10+n%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cleq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10+n%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cleq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10+n%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \| \tilde t \tilde \phi(a_1) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}}, \dots, \| \tilde t \tilde \phi(a_n) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \leq \frac{1}{10 n^2}" class="latex"></p>

Thus, by the triangle inequality, we have </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D+-+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10n%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D+-+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10n%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5C%7C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D+-+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10n%5E2%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \| \tilde t \tilde \phi(a_1) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}}, \dots, \| \tilde t \tilde \phi(a_n) \|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \geq \frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{10n^2}" class="latex"></p>
<p> for a set <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+t%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+t%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+t%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\tilde t}" class="latex"> of reals of density <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\gg n^{-O(n)}}" class="latex">.</p>
<p>
Applying a smooth Fourier multiplier of Littlewood-Paley type, one can find a trigonometric polynomial </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Ceta%28x%29+%3D+%5Csum_%7Bm%3A+%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0+n%2F10%7D%7D+b_m+e%5E%7B2%5Cpi+i+mx%7D+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Ceta%28x%29+%3D+%5Csum_%7Bm%3A+%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0+n%2F10%7D%7D+b_m+e%5E%7B2%5Cpi+i+mx%7D+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Ceta%28x%29+%3D+%5Csum_%7Bm%3A+%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0+n%2F10%7D%7D+b_m+e%5E%7B2%5Cpi+i+mx%7D+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \eta(x) = \sum_{m: |m| \leq n^{C_0 n/10}} b_m e^{2\pi i mx} " class="latex"></p>
<p> which takes values in <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5B0%2C1%5D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5B0%2C1%5D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5B0%2C1%5D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{[0,1]}" class="latex">, is <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cgg+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cgg+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cgg+1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\gg 1}" class="latex"> for <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5C%7Cx%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D+-+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10n%5E2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5C%7Cx%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D+-+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10n%5E2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5C%7Cx%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cgeq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D+-+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B10n%5E2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\|x\|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \geq \frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{10n^2}}" class="latex">, and is no larger than <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BO%28+n%5E%7B-100+C_0n%7D+%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BO%28+n%5E%7B-100+C_0n%7D+%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7BO%28+n%5E%7B-100+C_0n%7D+%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{O( n^{-100 C_0n} )}" class="latex"> for <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5C%7Cx%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cleq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5C%7Cx%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cleq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5C%7Cx%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D+%5Cleq+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\|x\|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}} \leq \frac{1}{n+1}}" class="latex">. We then have </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+%5Cprod_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5En+%5Ceta%28+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_j%29+%29+%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+%5Cprod_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5En+%5Ceta%28+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_j%29+%29+%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+%5Cprod_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5En+%5Ceta%28+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_j%29+%29+%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \mathop{\bf E}_t \prod_{j=1}^n \eta( t \tilde \phi(a_j) ) \gg n^{-O(n)} " class="latex"></p>
<p> where <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+f%28t%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+f%28t%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+f%28t%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\mathop{\bf E}_t f(t)}" class="latex"> denotes the mean value of a quasiperiodic function <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bf%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bf%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bf%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{f}" class="latex"> on the reals <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{{\bf R}}" class="latex">. We expand the left-hand side out as </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+m_1+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+0%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+m_1+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+0%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+m_1+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+0%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D.&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \sum_{m_1,\dots,m_n: m_1 \tilde \phi(a_1) + \dots + m_n \tilde \phi(a_n) = 0} b_{m_1} \dots b_{m_n}." class="latex"></p>
<p> From the genericity of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+w_1%2C%5Cdots%2C%5Ctilde+w_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+w_1%2C%5Cdots%2C%5Ctilde+w_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ctilde+w_1%2C%5Cdots%2C%5Ctilde+w_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\tilde w_1,\dots,\tilde w_n}" class="latex">, we see that the constraint </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+0+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+0+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+0+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  m_1 \tilde \phi(a_1) + \dots + m_n \tilde \phi(a_n) = 0 " class="latex"></p>
<p> occurs if and only if <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bm_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bm_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bm_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{m_1 a_1 + \dots + m_n a_n}" class="latex"> is a scalar multiple of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_n-a_1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_n-a_1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Ba_n-a_1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{a_n-a_1}" class="latex">, or equivalently (by <a href="#aa">(1)</a>, <a href="#cc">(2)</a>) an integer multiple of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{(c'_1,\dots,c'_d)}" class="latex">. Thus <a name="big"></a></p><a name="big">
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+m_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D+%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D+%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D.+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%283%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+m_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D+%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D+%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D.+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%283%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+m_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D+%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D+%5Cgg+n%5E%7B-O%28n%29%7D.+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%283%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \sum_{m_1,\dots,m_n: m_1 a_1 + \dots + m_n a_n \in {\bf Z} (c'_1,\dots,c'_d)} b_{m_1} \dots b_{m_n} \gg n^{-O(n)}. \ \ \ \ \ (3)" class="latex"></p>
</a><p><a name="big"></a> Next, we consider the average <a name="lad"></a></p><a name="lad">
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+%5Cvarphi%28+t+%5Cxi+%29+%5Cprod_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5En+%5Ceta%28+t+v_j+%29+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%284%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+%5Cvarphi%28+t+%5Cxi+%29+%5Cprod_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5En+%5Ceta%28+t+v_j+%29+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%284%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cmathop%7B%5Cbf+E%7D_t+%5Cvarphi%28+t+%5Cxi+%29+%5Cprod_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5En+%5Ceta%28+t+v_j+%29+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%284%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \mathop{\bf E}_t \varphi( t \xi ) \prod_{j=1}^n \eta( t v_j ) \ \ \ \ \ (4)" class="latex"></p>
</a><p><a name="lad"></a> where <a name="xiw"></a></p><a name="xiw">
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cxi+%3A%3D+c%27_1+w_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+c%27_d+w_d.+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%285%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cxi+%3A%3D+c%27_1+w_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+c%27_d+w_d.+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%285%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Cxi+%3A%3D+c%27_1+w_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+c%27_d+w_d.+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%285%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \xi := c'_1 w_1 + \dots + c'_d w_d. \ \ \ \ \ (5)" class="latex"></p>
</a><p><a name="xiw"></a> and <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\varphi}" class="latex"> is the Dirichlet series </p>

<p> By Fourier expansion and writing <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_j+%3D+%5Cphi%28a_j%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_j+%3D+%5Cphi%28a_j%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bv_j+%3D+%5Cphi%28a_j%29%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{v_j = \phi(a_j)}" class="latex">, we may write <a href="#lad">(4)</a> as </p>
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm%2Cm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0n%2F2%7D%3B+m_1+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+m+%5Cxi%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D.+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm%2Cm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0n%2F2%7D%3B+m_1+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+m+%5Cxi%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D.+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++%5Csum_%7Bm%2Cm_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cm_n%3A+%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0n%2F2%7D%3B+m_1+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+m+%5Cxi%7D+b_%7Bm_1%7D+%5Cdots+b_%7Bm_n%7D.+&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  \sum_{m,m_1,\dots,m_n: |m| \leq n^{C_0n/2}; m_1 \phi(a_1) + \dots + m_n \phi(a_n) = m \xi} b_{m_1} \dots b_{m_n}. " class="latex"></p>
<p> The support of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bb_%7Bm_i%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bb_%7Bm_i%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bb_%7Bm_i%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{b_{m_i}}" class="latex"> implies that <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7Cm_i%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0n%2F10%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7Cm_i%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0n%2F10%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7Cm_i%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0n%2F10%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{|m_i| \leq n^{C_0n/10}}" class="latex">. <p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+m+%5Cxi+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%286%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+m+%5Cxi+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%286%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+%5Cphi%28a_1%29+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+%5Cphi%28a_n%29+%3D+m+%5Cxi+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%286%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  m_1 \phi(a_1) + \dots + m_n \phi(a_n) = m \xi \ \ \ \ \ (6)" class="latex"></p>
</a><p><a name="slob"></a> implies that <a name="maa"></a></p><a name="maa">
<p align="center"><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D+%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%287%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D+%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%287%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cdisplaystyle++m_1+a_1+%2B+%5Cdots+%2B+m_n+a_n+%5Cin+%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D+%28c%27_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cc%27_d%29+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%5C+%287%29&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\displaystyle  m_1 a_1 + \dots + m_n a_n \in {\bf Z} (c'_1,\dots,c'_d) \ \ \ \ \ (7)" class="latex"></p>
</a><p><a name="maa"></a> and conversely that <a href="#maa">(7)</a> implies that <a href="#slob">(6)</a> holds for some <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bm%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bm%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bm%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{m}" class="latex"> with <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0+n%2F2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0+n%2F2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%7Cm%7C+%5Cleq+n%5E%7BC_0+n%2F2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{|m| \leq n^{C_0 n/2}}" class="latex">. From <a href="#big">(3)</a> we thus have </p>

<p> In particular, there exists a <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bt%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{t}" class="latex"> such that </p>

" class="latex"></p>
<p> Since <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cvarphi%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\varphi}" class="latex"> is bounded in magnitude by <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BC_0n%2F2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BC_0n%2F2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7Bn%5E%7BC_0n%2F2%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{n^{C_0n/2}}" class="latex">, and <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ceta%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ceta%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Ceta%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\eta}" class="latex"> is bounded by <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=000000&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{1}" class="latex">, we thus have </p>

			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Bogdan's avatar" src="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32 wp-hovercard-attachment grav-hashed grav-hijack" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>You proved that if the conjecture is false for a given n, then it false for SOME v_1, …, v_n of size n^(Cn^2). Can similar methods to be extended to prove a stronger result, that if the conjecture is false for a given n, then it false for MANY v_1, …, v_n of size n^(Cn^2), say, for a positive proportion (independent of n) of all tuples v_1, …, v_n of this size. Then, for the first unproved case n=8, we could check the conjecture for some RANDOM tuples bouded by 8^64C (if C is not too lagre), and, if true, confirm the original conjecture for n=8, with probability, arbitrary closed to 1.</p>

			<p class="comment-permalink"><a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2015/05/13/a-remark-on-the-lonely-runner-conjecture/#comment-455758" title="Permalink to this comment">14 May, 2015 at 10:28 am</a></p>
			<p class="comment-author"><strong class="fn"><a href="http://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao" class="url" rel="ugc external nofollow">Terence Tao</a></strong></p>
					</div>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Terence Tao's avatar" src="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32 wp-hovercard-attachment grav-hashed grav-hijack" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>One can certainly establish the conjecture for “most” choices of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="v_1,\dots,v_n" class="latex">; for instance, if the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="v_1,\dots,v_n" class="latex"> are linearly independent over <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cbf+Q%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cbf+Q%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cbf+Q%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\bf Q}" class="latex"> (which occurs for almost every choice of reals <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="v_1,\dots,v_n" class="latex">), then the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5C%7Ctv_i%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5C%7Ctv_i%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5C%7Ctv_i%5C%7C_%7B%7B%5Cbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cbf+Z%7D%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\|tv_i\|_{{\bf R}/{\bf Z}}" class="latex"> behave as independent random variables and the claim is quite easy to show in this case.  However, all of the difficulty of the problem is concentrated in “special” choices of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_1%2C%5Cdots%2Cv_n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="v_1,\dots,v_n" class="latex">, and knowing that the conjecture is true for “most” choices doesn’t make much impact on this most difficult case.  (An analogy is with Fermat’s last theorem: it is easy to show that the equation <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=a%5En%2Bb%5En%3Dc%5En&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=a%5En%2Bb%5En%3Dc%5En&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=a%5En%2Bb%5En%3Dc%5En&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="a^n+b^n=c^n" class="latex"> is false for “most” choices of $a,b,c,n$, for just about any notion of “most”, but this does not really make a dent in solving the problem.)</p>

			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Bogdan's avatar" src="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/104e89dc48297ce754889638da3d5e4d5947e047b40d3a6c05b9f923edf2afd3?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32 wp-hovercard-attachment grav-hashed grav-hijack" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>You completely misundersood my comment :) I wil try again.<br>
Your theorem is: If there is at least one counterexample for ANY v_1, …, v_n, then there is at least ONE counterexample for bounded v_1, …, v_n.<br>
Now, assume we have a stronger result, namely:<br>
Statement A: If there is at least one counterexample for any v_1, …, v_n, then positive proportion of ALL bounded v_1, …, v_n are all counterexamples.<br>
Then, trying at random, we could rule out a possibility that positive proportion of ALL bounded v_1, …, v_n are all counterexamples, and<br>
use statement A to prove the result in full.</p>
<p>Example how this may work. </p>
<p>Statement B: If there is at least one counterexample N to odd Goldbach’s conjecture, then at least N/log N even numbers in the region from 2 to N are ALL counterexamples to even Goldbach’s conjecture.</p>
<p>Proof is trivial. If N is a counterexample to odd Goldbach’s conjecture, then N-p is a counterexample to the even Goldbach’s conjecture for any odd p less than N.</p>
<p>Now, we can check even Goldbach’s conjecture for sufficiently many random numbers below exp(3100), and the odd Goldbach’s conjecture for numbers below exp(3100) follows from statement B. See <a href="https://rjlipton.wordpress.com/2014/06/06/is-this-a-proof-2/" rel="nofollow ugc">https://rjlipton.wordpress.com/2014/06/06/is-this-a-proof-2/</a> for a variant of this argument.</p>

			<p class="comment-author"><strong class="fn"><a href="http://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao" class="url" rel="ugc external nofollow">Terence Tao</a></strong></p>
					</div>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Terence Tao's avatar" src="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32 wp-hovercard-attachment grav-hashed grav-hijack" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>Ah, I see what you are saying now.  I doubt that this sort of “counterexample dispersion” effect is present in this problem; roughly speaking, the only symmetry we have available in this problem to convert one counterexample into many counterexamples are Freiman homomorphisms.  (There is a technicality here in that there is some loss in the lower bound on runner separation every time one applies such a homomorphism, based on the quality of that homomorphism, but let me ignore this technicality for sake of current discussions.)  There are enough homomorphisms present to “rectify” any finite set of speeds into a set of bounded integers, but not enough to obtain a positive proportion of such sets.  As mentioned in my previous comment, for randomly selected sets of speeds (which all lie, more or less, in a single Freiman isomorphism class) the claim is trivial to prove, but this does not have much bearing on all the other Freiman isomorphism classes (and if the conjecture is to fail, it is likely to come from a very special, carefully constructed, Freiman isomorphism class, which will not be detectable by random search).</p>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Unknown's avatar" src="https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>Correction: In conjecture 1 (to be exactly equivalent to conjecture 2), it seems that “different speeds” should be interpreted as “there is at least one runner whose speed is different from the speeds of the other runners”.</p>

	<div class="comment odd alt thread-odd thread-alt depth-1 vcard" id="comment-455887">
		<div class="comment-metadata">
			<p class="comment-permalink"><a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2015/05/13/a-remark-on-the-lonely-runner-conjecture/#comment-455887" title="Permalink to this comment">15 May, 2015 at 8:05 am</a></p>
			<p class="comment-author"><strong class="fn">Anonymous</strong></p>
					</div>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Unknown's avatar" src="https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>The simple identity <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+%7C%7C+x+%7C%7C%29+%3D+%7C+%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+x%29%7C&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+%7C%7C+x+%7C%7C%29+%3D+%7C+%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+x%29%7C&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+%7C%7C+x+%7C%7C%29+%3D+%7C+%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+x%29%7C&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\sin (\pi || x ||) = | \sin (\pi x)|" class="latex"> implies that conjecture 2 has the following analytic formulation </p>
<p><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cmax_%7Bt+%5Cin+%5Cmathbb+R%7D+%5Cmin_%7B1%5Cleq++j+%5Cleq+n%7D+%7Csin%28%5Cpi+t+v_j%29%7C+%5Cgeq+%5Csin+%5Cfrac+%7B%5Cpi%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cmax_%7Bt+%5Cin+%5Cmathbb+R%7D+%5Cmin_%7B1%5Cleq++j+%5Cleq+n%7D+%7Csin%28%5Cpi+t+v_j%29%7C+%5Cgeq+%5Csin+%5Cfrac+%7B%5Cpi%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cmax_%7Bt+%5Cin+%5Cmathbb+R%7D+%5Cmin_%7B1%5Cleq++j+%5Cleq+n%7D+%7Csin%28%5Cpi+t+v_j%29%7C+%5Cgeq+%5Csin+%5Cfrac+%7B%5Cpi%7D%7Bn%2B1%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\max_{t \in \mathbb R} \min_{1\leq  j \leq n} |sin(\pi t v_j)| \geq \sin \frac {\pi}{n+1}" class="latex"> </p>
<p>It is easy to verify that the (outer) maximum is attained at an intersection point of two sine curves (with corresponding velocities <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_i%2C+v_j&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_i%2C+v_j&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_i%2C+v_j&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="v_i, v_j" class="latex">), i.e. </p>
<p><img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7C%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+t+v_i%29%7C+%3D+%7C%5Csin%28%5Cpi+t+v_j%29%7C&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7C%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+t+v_i%29%7C+%3D+%7C%5Csin%28%5Cpi+t+v_j%29%7C&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7C%5Csin+%28%5Cpi+t+v_i%29%7C+%3D+%7C%5Csin%28%5Cpi+t+v_j%29%7C&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="|\sin (\pi t v_i)| = |\sin(\pi t v_j)|" class="latex"> for some <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_i%2C+v_j&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_i%2C+v_j&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=v_i%2C+v_j&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="v_i, v_j" class="latex"> </p>
<p>Implying that <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="t" class="latex"> is rational (a multiple of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F%28v_i+-+v_j%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F%28v_i+-+v_j%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F%28v_i+-+v_j%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="1/(v_i - v_j)" class="latex"> or <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F%28v_i+%2B+v_j%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F%28v_i+%2B+v_j%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F%28v_i+%2B+v_j%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="1/(v_i + v_j)" class="latex">). </p>
<p>Therefore (without loss of generality) <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="t" class="latex"> may be assumed to be rational (with denominator being the sum or difference of two integer velocities).</p>

	<div class="comment odd alt thread-odd thread-alt depth-1 vcard parent" id="comment-455911">
		<div class="comment-metadata">
			<p class="comment-permalink"><a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2015/05/13/a-remark-on-the-lonely-runner-conjecture/#comment-455911" title="Permalink to this comment">16 May, 2015 at 9:18 am</a></p>
			<p class="comment-author"><strong class="fn">Drive by shooting</strong></p>
					</div>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Unknown's avatar" src="https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://0.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>Would you buy this argument?</p>
<p>We can generalize the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="n" class="latex"> velocities to be arbitrary real numbers, for example by choosing a frame of reference traveling with an arbitrary runner. The system then satisfies the constraints of the Poincare recurrence theorem, for the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="n" class="latex"> positions, and the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="n" class="latex"> velocities. But any group of $n-1$ runners must then also fulfill the constraints of the Poincare recurrence theorem. Thus, fix a reference frame to an arbitrary runner, and consider a volume of the position space of the remaining <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="n-1" class="latex"> runners, of length <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cepsilon+%5Cin+%280%2C+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cepsilon+%5Cin+%280%2C+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cepsilon+%5Cin+%280%2C+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\epsilon \in (0, \frac{1}{2})" class="latex"> for each of the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="n-1" class="latex"> runners, and exactly opposite to the origin of the chosen runner. By the Poincare recurrence theorem the <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=n-1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="n-1" class="latex"> runners must revisit this volume infinitely often. We then have for any <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cepsilon+%5Cin+%280%2C+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cepsilon+%5Cin+%280%2C+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Cepsilon+%5Cin+%280%2C+%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\epsilon \in (0, \frac{1}{2})" class="latex"> each runner is separated from all the other runners by that amount infinitely often.</p>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="James Smith's avatar" src="https://2.gravatar.com/avatar/534134bdb8695805dc9b8970472da7f0d0259849dbdbccaa4f47843e72a18404?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://2.gravatar.com/avatar/534134bdb8695805dc9b8970472da7f0d0259849dbdbccaa4f47843e72a18404?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://2.gravatar.com/avatar/534134bdb8695805dc9b8970472da7f0d0259849dbdbccaa4f47843e72a18404?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://2.gravatar.com/avatar/534134bdb8695805dc9b8970472da7f0d0259849dbdbccaa4f47843e72a18404?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://2.gravatar.com/avatar/534134bdb8695805dc9b8970472da7f0d0259849dbdbccaa4f47843e72a18404?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://2.gravatar.com/avatar/534134bdb8695805dc9b8970472da7f0d0259849dbdbccaa4f47843e72a18404?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32 wp-hovercard-attachment grav-hashed grav-hijack" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>A small thing that confused me: you say in your definition of the problem that all the runners start at the origin. To say they start at the same place might be a little clearer. And I wonder now I come to think of it if the circle were indeed replaced with a disc how the problem would unfold.</p>
<p><i>[<img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cmathbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cmathbf+Z%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cmathbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cmathbf+Z%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%7B%5Cmathbf+R%7D%2F%7B%5Cmathbf+Z%7D&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="{\mathbf R}/{\mathbf Z}" class="latex"> denotes the additive unit circle, rather than the multiplicative (or geometric) unit circle <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=S%5E1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=S%5E1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=S%5E1&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="S^1" class="latex"> – one can think of it as the geometric unit circle transformed by a logarithmic change of variables.  In particular, the identity element 1 of the multiplicative unit circle becomes the identity element 0 of the additive unit circle. -T.]</i></p>

		<div class="comment-metadata">
			<p class="comment-permalink"><a href="https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2015/05/13/a-remark-on-the-lonely-runner-conjecture/#comment-455932" title="Permalink to this comment">17 May, 2015 at 7:33 pm</a></p>
			<p class="comment-author"><strong class="fn">victor</strong></p>
					</div>

The deterministic problem is the limiting case where $\mu = 0$ and $\sigma= \infty$.  Would it make sense to solve the stochastic problem first?</p>

The difficulty in this conjecture lies not with such “generic” situations, but rather with very special “arithmetically structured” situations in which the runner velocities all have a rigid relationship with each other (e.g. they are all rational multiples of each other with small height).</p>

			<p class="comment-author"><strong class="fn"><a href="http://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao" class="url" rel="ugc external nofollow">Terence Tao</a></strong></p>
					</div>

		<div class="comment-content">
			<img referrerpolicy="no-referrer" alt="Terence Tao's avatar" src="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG" srcset="https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=32&d=identicon&r=PG 1x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=48&d=identicon&r=PG 1.5x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=64&d=identicon&r=PG 2x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=96&d=identicon&r=PG 3x, https://1.gravatar.com/avatar/d7f0e4a42bbbf58ffa656c92d4a32b2b6752e802dfa4cb919e5774dcfda006c0?s=128&d=identicon&r=PG 4x" class="avatar avatar-32 wp-hovercard-attachment grav-hashed grav-hijack" height="32" width="32" loading="lazy" decoding="async">			<p>Cover the n-torus by <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=O%28n%5E%7BO%28n%29%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=O%28n%5E%7BO%28n%29%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=O%28n%5E%7BO%28n%29%7D%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="O(n^{O(n)})" class="latex"> boxes of sidelength <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F20n%5E2&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F20n%5E2&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=1%2F20n%5E2&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="1/20n^2" class="latex">.  By the Dirichlet box principle (pigeonhole principle), one of these boxes will contain <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%28%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Cphi%28a_n%29%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%28%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Cphi%28a_n%29%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%28%5Ctilde+t+%5Ctilde+%5Cphi%28a_1%29%2C+%5Cdots%2C+%5Ctilde+t+%5Cphi%28a_n%29%29&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="(\tilde t \tilde \phi(a_1), \dots, \tilde t \phi(a_n))" class="latex"> for a set of <img src="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Ctilde+t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002" srcset="https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Ctilde+t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002 1x, https://s0.wp.com/latex.php?latex=%5Ctilde+t&bg=ffffff&fg=545454&s=0&c=20201002&zoom=4.5 4x" alt="\tilde t" class="latex"> of positive density.  Now subtract to get the claim.  (This argument is identical to the one used to prove the usual Dirichlet approximation theorem.  There are some technical issues regarding the nature of density used here, but by using some equidistribution theory one can show that all the usual notions of density (lower Banach, upper Banach, etc.) agree for the sets in question.)</p>
